descriptionChirho: Causative active destruction of people, cities, or lands, corresponding to Arabic أَهْلَكَ/يُهْلِكُ (ahlaka) and Korean 멸하다/파괴하다, the dominant sense of the Hifil stem across all inflections.
Intensive active destruction or ruination, corresponding to Arabic أَهْلَكَ/أَتْلَفَ and Korean 멸하다/파괴하다/파멸하다, the Piel intensive counterpart of Hifil destruction.
Moral or behavioral corruption in the Hifil stem, corresponding to Arabic أَفْسَدَ/يُفْسِدُ (afsada/yufsidu) and Korean 타락하다/부패하다, describing corrupt conduct rather than physical annihilation.
Intensive moral corruption or perversion of what is good in the Piel stem, corresponding to Arabic أَفْسَدَ (afsada) and Korean 타락시키다/부패하게 하다, actively causing moral ruin.
Passive or reflexive becoming corrupt or ruined, corresponding to Arabic فَسَدَ/فَسَدَتْ (fasada, intransitive) and Korean 부패했다/황폐해졌다, describing the state of being corrupted.

Causative passive indicating something rendered defective or blemished, corresponding to Arabic مُفْسَد (mufsad, passive participle) and Korean 더럽혀진/상한, used of sacrificial animals or polluted things.

Causing something to go to waste or be squandered, corresponding to Arabic أَضَاعَ/أَتْلَفَ and Korean 망가뜨리다/헛되리라, a nuance of ruination focused on wasting rather than violent destruction or moral corruption.
